dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies, commercial space operators, and academic or nonprofit entities engaged in space activities.
dimensions.evidence: eligible entity means-- (A) a United States-based-- (i) non-Federal, commercial entity; (ii) institution of higher education... or (iii) nonprofit organization

dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts participating commercial entities via competitive awards and changes federal guidance and future regulations for space operations.
dimensions.evidence: establish a demonstration project to make competitive awards for the research, development, and demonstration of technologies leading to the remediation of selected orbital debris

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes $150 million in appropriations for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Administrator to carry out this section $150,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Requires new agency lists, interagency standard practice updates, and federal contracting authorities for remediation services.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary, in consultation with the Administrator... shall publish a list of select identified orbital debris

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing reporting requirements, periodic reviews every 5 years, and authorized funding running through 2030.
dimensions.evidence: Not less frequently than every 5 years, the Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices referred to in subsection (a) shall be assessed and, if necessary, updated

importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes an orbital debris remediation demonstration project at NASA authorized at $150 million, updates orbital debris mitigation standard practices across federal agencies, and facilitates space traffic coordination standards.
